titulo: Subjunctive: wishes, doubt and emotion: Emotion and judgement

aula.objetivo: Use the present subjunctive after verbs of wishing, asking and advising («quiero que vengas»), of doubt and denial («no creo que venga», «dudo que…») and of emotion and judgement («me alegra que…», «es importante que…»), and tell it apart from the indicative.

itens.pt: I'm sorry that, it saddens me that

blocos.titulo: Feelings and opinions take the subjunctive
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: when you react to something — joy, sadness, surprise, annoyance — or give a judgement, the next verb goes in the subjunctive, even if the fact is true: «Me alegra que estés aquí» (I'm glad you're here — you ARE here, and I'm glad about it). English uses the indicative ("you're here"); Spanish uses the subjunctive because the main point is your reaction. STEP 2: expressions of emotion: «me alegra que, me gusta que, me encanta que, me molesta que, me sorprende que, me da pena que, me da rabia que, siento que, tengo miedo de que». STEP 3: impersonal judgements: «es bueno, es malo, es importante, es necesario, es normal, es raro, es mejor, es increíble, es una pena» + «que» + subjunctive: «Es importante que descanses» (It's important that you rest / for you to rest). STEP 4: if the subject is the same, use the infinitive: «Me alegra verte» or «Me alegro de verte» (I'm glad to see you). If the subjects change, use «que» + subjunctive: «Me alegro de que vengas» (I'm glad you're coming). STEP 5: careful with «siento que». Meaning "I'm sorry that", it takes the subjunctive («Siento que no puedas venir»). Meaning "I feel / sense that", it takes the indicative («Siento que estás cansado»). STEP 6: remember the contrast with certainty: «es verdad que» and «es evidente que» take the indicative, while «es raro que» and «es una pena que» take the subjunctive. STEP 7: in Latin America, say «Me alegra que vengan» instead of «que vengáis».
blocos.comparacao: English "I'm glad you're here", "It's a shame you can't come", "It's important for you to rest" use the indicative or an infinitive. Spanish uses the subjunctive after any reaction or judgement, even about a true fact: «Me alegra que estés aquí», «Es una pena que no puedas venir», «Es importante que descanses».

exemplos.pt: It bothers me that you're late.

exemplos.ru: Es una pena que no puedas venir.
exemplos.pt: It's a shame you can't come.
It surprises me that he knows so much.

erros.motivo: After verbs of emotion, the verb goes in the subjunctive (unlike English "I'm glad you ARE here").
A judgement with «es importante que» takes the subjunctive.

erros.errado: Me alegra que yo estar aquí.
erros.motivo: With the same subject, use the infinitive.
«Es evidente que» states a fact, so the verb stays in the indicative.

blocos.titulo: Una carta a una amiga / A letter to a friend
blocos.ru: Querida Sofía: Me alegra mucho que por fin te mudes a Madrid. Sé que estabas nerviosa y es normal que tengas un poco de miedo, pero no creo que tengas problemas para adaptarte: eres una persona abierta, y a la gente le encanta que hables con ella. Es importante que busques un piso cerca del metro, y te aconsejo que lo veas en persona antes de firmar. Mi hermano dice que conoce a un casero muy amable y quiere que lo llames. Dudo que encuentres algo barato en el centro, pero es posible que en Lavapiés haya buenas opciones. Ojalá puedas venir a cenar a casa el sábado. Me da pena que ahora vivas tan lejos de tu familia, pero creo que te va a ir muy bien. Un abrazo, Lucía.
blocos.pt: Dear Sofía, I'm so glad you're finally moving to Madrid. I know you were nervous and it's normal to be a bit scared, but I don't think you'll have any trouble settling in: you're an open person, and people love it when you chat with them. It's important that you look for a flat near the metro, and I advise you to see it in person before you sign. My brother says he knows a very nice landlord and wants you to call him. I doubt you'll find anything cheap in the centre, but there may be good options in Lavapiés. I hope you can come for dinner at our place on Saturday. I'm sad that you'll be living so far from your family now, but I think it'll all go really well. Love, Lucía.

perguntas.resposta: Que Sofía se mude a Madrid.

perguntas.pergunta: ¿Qué le aconseja a Sofía sobre el piso?
perguntas.resposta: Que lo vea en persona antes de firmar.
Que Sofía encuentre algo barato en el centro.
Que Sofía pueda ir a cenar a su casa.

blocos.enunciado: Write a short note to a friend with four sentences: one of emotion («me alegra que…»), one of advice («te aconsejo que…»), one of doubt («dudo que…») and one of wishing («ojalá…»).
Say out loud two sentences with «creo que», two with «no creo que» and two with «dudo que». Pay attention to the mood of the verb.
